title: The ongoing conflict between North and South Sudan, particularly over the oil-rich Darfur region, has escalated following the withdrawal of the Sudan People's Liberation Movement (SPLM) from the national government and the commencement of peace talks in Libya. The SPLM's departure highlights the failure of the comprehensive peace agreement (CPA) signed in 2005, which has not been effectively implemented by the Sudanese government. Key issues include unfilled government positions, control over oil revenues, unresolved border delimitation, unilateral decision-making by the Khartoum government, and widespread non-compliance with CPA provisions. These challenges raise concerns about the future of peace and stability in Sudan.
